# Wiki maintenance

[Wiki home](README.md) | [Edit source](../../AGENTS.md)

## Living wiki (mandatory)

- The wiki lives in [Docs/Wiki](../../Docs/Wiki/README.md), versioned with the code. This file (`AGENTS.md`, plural) is the technical wiki's source of truth; do not create a separate `agent.md` or duplicate instructions in `CLAUDE.md`. The player handbook has its own source, described below.
- At the start of a task, read the relevant sections here and the affected implementation. Before finishing any change to gameplay, architecture, setup, tooling, assets, tests or known limitations, update the affected facts here in the same change. Record new gotchas and reusable test helpers. Update `README.md` for player-facing changes and `Assets/Design/DESIGN.md` for agreed design changes.
- Distinguish implemented behavior, planned design and verified results. Only claim tests actually run; date a status entry when its facts were checked. Roadmap #53 remains the only source for work order; do not copy its checklist into the wiki.
- Regenerate the wiki with `python3 Tools/Docs/build_wiki.py`, then verify with `python3 Tools/Docs/build_wiki.py --check`. Commit the source and generated pages together. Never edit generated wiki pages directly. When adding or renaming a level-two section here, update the generator's page mapping if needed; every section must appear in the wiki.
- Claude and other agents perform this maintenance during repository tasks. There is no unattended AI service or scheduled Claude job. CI checks that the wiki matches this file; it cannot prove that prose matches the implementation.
- Keep developer documentation in this repository so reviews, history and branches include it. A future published site should render these same sources. Keep player guides in `README.md` and asset licences in `Assets/_Project/Art/CREDITS.md`.
- Visual reader: open `Docs/Wiki/index.html` directly in a browser (offline, no server/dependencies). It has navigation, full-text search, an article outline, light/dark themes and expandable references. `Tools/Docs/reader.html` is its template; `Tools/Docs/wiki_reader.py` renders technical Markdown; `Tools/Docs/wiki_content.json` holds curated introductions, flows and captioned screenshots. These are sources; the generated HTML is checked by the same `--check` command.
- Visual documentation is part of maintenance: when a visible feature changes, add or replace relevant screenshots in `Docs/screenshots/<issue>/`, select them in `wiki_content.json` and explain what they show. Use descriptive alt text and captions with issue/context; label historical images and don't present older assets as the current art reference. Keep overview claims aligned with this file and don't claim a new screenshot or test without capturing/running it. Missing image files fail generation. Editorial summaries supplement the technical source; update both when their facts change.
- Player handbook (default landing view, 2026-10-17): `Tools/Docs/player_guide.json` contains seven German, task-oriented guides: first expedition, controls/HUD, exploration/survival, equipment/crafting/trading, Nostos/crew, travel and help/death/saving. `#home` opens player content; `#developer` opens the existing technical index. Both are generated to HTML and Markdown. Keep player instructions concrete (where to go, what key/button to use, prerequisites, what happens next), with numbered steps, visual grouping and captioned screenshots; developer details belong in the separate developer area. Preserve the distinction between normal ship Fuel, Exotic Matter in the warp tank, and Salvage.
- When gameplay, controls or menu labels change, update the affected handbook guides in the same change. Check actual implementation as well as these notes; each guide records evidence paths and a source-check date. Do not turn planned behavior into a playable instruction. In particular, the current code supports automatic cryo respawn; no manual crew-revive interaction was found. Lobby start labels are Start Mission / New Loop, and working on the shared drive requires the Nostos while it exists. Sources were checked, not a new playthrough.
- Wiki tooling checks: `python3 Tools/Docs/test_wiki.py` covers stale output, missing images/captions, unmapped source sections, player-guide links/evidence and safe reference rendering. CI runs it alongside `--check`. After reader interaction or CSS changes, also inspect desktop/mobile navigation, search, image enlargement and reference expansion in a browser; Unity tests are unnecessary for documentation-only changes.
